title: Plural partitive of common -is words
summary: For these -is words, use the strong consonants and replace -is with -iita/-iitä: kaunis (“beautiful”) → kauniita.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

For this selected kaunis-type family, replace final -is with -iita/-iitä. Both i letters are needed. In raitis, strengthen t to tt first. This is not a rule for every -is word: word-family membership must be learned.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: The word’s meaning stays connected to “beautiful”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not assume every -is word follows this family.
